problem_statement: When an XSD sequence contains multiple element particles that reference the same abstract declaration, name-based deduplication drops every reference after the first and loses that particle's occurrence constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Each repeated reference to the same abstract element produces a separate abstract wrapper field.
The wrappers have stable unique internal names while each keeps the abstract declaration's display name for the UI.
Each wrapper preserves minOccurs and maxOccurs from its own referencing particle; the focused two-reference fixture preserves maxOccurs values 1 and unbounded.
Existing concrete-element deduplication and the rest of the focused abstract-element suite remain green.
constraints: Do not add dependencies, change public APIs, edit CI, update documentation, lockfiles, generated output, or version numbers.

Keep the change limited to packages/ui/src/services/document/xml-schema/xml-schema-document.service.ts and a new focused test at packages/ui/src/services/document/xml-schema/xml-schema-document.service.abstract-repeated-ref.test.ts.
Do not redesign substitution-group membership, schema-path indexing, ordinary concrete-element deduplication, or unrelated DataMapper UI behavior.
Use an inline deterministic XSD fixture; do not add fixture files or require network access.
implementation_hints: The current same-name guard in populateElement runs before abstract-element dispatch; repeated abstract references need to reach populateAbstractElement while ordinary concrete duplicates should keep their existing behavior.
Give each sibling abstract wrapper a stable collision-free internal name derived from repository-native sibling context, and continue using the resolved declaration name as displayName.
Add one focused Vitest file using the maintainer's two-reference shape and assert wrapper count, unique names, preserved display names, and per-particle cardinality.
process_requirements: A human must review, approve, and sign all AI-generated code; the AI agent may not submit the pull request independently.
Use a contributor-created descriptive branch on a fork; never push to another contributor's branch.
Before submission run the UI lint, style lint, and test commands required by AGENTS.md.
Keep under 10 pull requests per operator per day and provide active human follow-up within two weeks.
AI-use disclosure is optional but recommended.

acceptance_contract.problem: When a sequence contains multiple element particles referencing the same abstract declaration, the name-and-namespace deduplication guard returns before constructing the later abstract wrapper, losing that particle and its occurrence constraints.
expected_behavior: Every repeated reference to the abstract declaration produces a distinct abstract wrapper field.
Each wrapper preserves its own minOccurs and maxOccurs values from its referencing particle.
The abstract declaration's display name remains visible to the UI.
The supplied two-reference shape yields two wrappers rather than one.
non_goals: No new option, flag, or public API.
No redesign of substitution-group membership behavior.
No unrelated change to ordinary concrete-element deduplication or UI presentation.

design_evidence.summary: The member-authored issue identifies the same-name deduplication root cause, requires one wrapper per abstract reference with particle-specific occurrence constraints, and requires preserving the UI display name.

oracle.base_failure_contains: should create a unique wrapper with its own cardinality for each abstract element ref
